title: OpenSHMEM MLIR: A Dialect for Compile-Time Optimization of One-Sided Communications
problem: Communication is a growing bottleneck in HPC, but mainstream compilers lose communication intent through opaque runtime calls. OpenSHMEM one-sided PGAS model has rich semantics but they are not preserved for compiler optimization.
motivation: Explicit communication semantics enable optimizations that are impossible to recover from low-level IR. One-sided communication patterns and memory model can guide compiler transformations to reduce latency and bandwidth.
method: Develop OpenSHMEM dialect for MLIR that preserves one-sided communication, symmetric memory, and team/context structures as first-class IR constructs. Integrate with existing MLIR/LLVM optimization passes. Demonstrate four specific transformations.
key_novelty: First MLIR dialect for OpenSHMEM preserving PGAS semantics; communication-aware optimization framework; four concrete optimizations (PE recording, atomic fusion, blocking-to-non-blocking conversion, message aggregation).
contributions: OpenSHMEM MLIR dialect capturing one-sided communication semantics
Four demonstrated transformations: PE counting, atomic fusion, operation conversion, message aggregation
hardware_target: Generic HPC systems with one-sided communication support
limitations: Abstract only; no performance numbers for transformations; unclear scalability of approach; limited to four example optimizations; evaluation not described.
